articles.title: Microsoft Entra pushes passkeys, tightens identity security
articles.summary: Microsoft has expanded its Entra identity suite by introducing phishing-resistant MFA for Linux desktops and furthering the adoption of passkeys to enhance zero-trust security. These updates aim to strengthen authentication processes across diverse operating environments.

articles.title: Sophos uncovers AI-powered malware lab built for EDR evasion
articles.summary: Sophos has identified a sophisticated threat actor utilizing an AI-powered framework to develop and test malware specifically designed to evade endpoint detection and response (EDR) systems. The framework includes techniques like Cobalt Strike profile manipulation to disguise malicious traffic as legitimate network activity.

articles.title: Operation FlutterBridge: macOS Malvertising Campaign Spreads New FlutterShell Backdoor
articles.summary: Operation FlutterBridge is a malvertising campaign targeting macOS users that distributes a new backdoor called FlutterShell developed using the Flutter framework.

articles.title: Red Hat npm packages compromised in new Mini Shai-Hulud malware wave
articles.summary: Attackers compromised over 30 Red Hat Cloud Services npm packages by hijacking a developer's GitHub account to inject malicious credential-stealing code. The incident represents a significant supply chain attack targeting developer environments.

articles.title: Pakistan-Linked SideCopy Targets Afghanistan Finance Ministry with Xeno RAT
articles.summary: The Pakistan-aligned threat group SideCopy is conducting a spear-phishing campaign targeting the Afghanistan Ministry of Finance using the Xeno RAT. The attack utilizes malicious LNK files delivered within ZIP archives to compromise government systems.

articles.title: KDE Linux security audit cuts kernel modules and unused packages
articles.summary: The KDE community conducted a security audit of its Linux distribution, resulting in the removal of unused packages and kernel modules to minimize the attack surface. This move follows recent security vulnerabilities discovered in the upstream Linux kernel.

articles.title: Cybanetix unveils Managed AI Service to secure users, models, and agents
articles.summary: Cybanetix has launched a Managed AI Service that integrates multiple security technologies to protect enterprise AI usage, governance, and embedded models. The service is supported by 24/7 SOC monitoring to provide rapid incident response for AI-related security threats.

articles.title: OpenAI brings frontier AI to existing AWS environments
articles.summary: OpenAI has integrated its frontier models into Amazon Bedrock, allowing AWS customers to deploy generative AI applications using native cloud security and governance controls.

articles.title: ENISA NIS360 2026: Progress Across the Board, But the Sectors That Matter Most Are Still Falling Short
articles.summary: The ENISA NIS360 2026 report indicates overall improvements in EU cybersecurity maturity, though critical sectors like health, water, rail, and space continue to face significant vulnerabilities. The report highlights that despite progress, these essential industries remain in the high-risk zone under the NIS2 directive.

articles.title: Sensitive government personnel data posted online, Spanish police arrest suspect
articles.summary: Spanish police have arrested a man in Granada for allegedly leaking the personal information of employees from multiple sensitive state institutions, including the National Police and the National Cybersecurity Institute. The suspect reportedly published this restricted data across various online platforms.

articles.title: GoDaddy found malware on 1,980 WordPress sites using Steam as C2 infrastructure
articles.summary: GoDaddy researchers identified a malware campaign infecting nearly 2,000 WordPress sites that utilizes Steam community profile comments as an unconventional command-and-control infrastructure. The malware retrieves hidden instructions from these profiles using invisible Unicode characters to execute malicious payloads.

articles.title: Cybersecurity jobs available right now: June 2, 2026
articles.summary: Google is seeking an Agentic Safety and Ecosystem Architect to develop security controls, permission models, and monitoring mechanisms for autonomous agents on the Android platform.

articles.title: Dashlane Discloses Brute-Force Attack, Encrypted Vaults of Fewer Than 20 Users Downloaded
articles.summary: Dashlane reported that fewer than 20 personal user accounts were compromised after an external threat actor conducted a brute-force attack targeting two-factor authentication. The attacker successfully downloaded the encrypted vaults of the affected accounts.

articles.title: Why Encrypted File Sharing Is Essential for Modern Businesses
articles.summary: Encrypted file sharing is presented as a critical defense mechanism for modern businesses to protect sensitive data and prevent corporate scandals. It emphasizes the necessity of securing digital communications to mitigate risks associated with data exposure.

articles.title: Attackers are exploiting Palo Alto Networks defect that initially flew under the radar
articles.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting a Palo Alto Networks vulnerability that was previously considered low-risk, highlighting a rapid escalation in threat severity. Organizations are urged to prioritize patching to mitigate potential compromise.

articles.title: Hackers hijack thousands of sites for ClickFix and FakeUpdate attacks
articles.summary: A threat actor known as DriveSurge is compromising thousands of websites to distribute malware via ClickFix and FakeUpdate social engineering techniques. The campaign relies on deceptive browser pop-ups to trick users into executing malicious code.

articles.title: Shai-Hulud malware worms Red Hat npm package versions downloaded 80K times a week
articles.summary: Malicious 'Shai-Hulud' malware has been discovered embedded in multiple Red Hat-related npm packages, accumulating 80,000 weekly downloads. The campaign involves worm-like propagation tactics targeting developer environments.

articles.title: Red Hat npm packages compromised to steal developer credentials
articles.summary: Attackers compromised over 30 npm packages within the '@redhat-cloud-services' namespace to distribute the Miasma credential-stealing malware. This supply-chain attack specifically targeted developer credentials.

articles.title: Spain arrests doxer leaking sensitive data of govt employees
articles.summary: Spanish authorities have arrested a suspect for leaking sensitive information belonging to government employees, including personnel from the National Cybersecurity Institute (INCIBE).

articles.title: Inspector general finds NIST mistakes have made vulnerability database ineffective
articles.summary: An inspector general report highlights that massive backlogs in NIST's National Vulnerability Database have significantly diminished the platform's reliability and utility for security professionals. This operational failure has left tens of thousands of vulnerabilities unprocessed, creating significant gaps in public security intelligence.

articles.title: Tina Peters, convicted in election-security breach, emerges defiant and vows legal fight
articles.summary: Former Colorado clerk Tina Peters, who was convicted for her role in an election-security breach, has emerged from prison vowing a continued legal battle after her sentence was commuted. Her actions involved unauthorized access to election equipment, sparking ongoing debates over election integrity and security.

articles.title: Election interlopers register 5K+ domains, hope to catch some voting phish
articles.summary: Threat actors have registered over 5,000 election-themed domains to facilitate phishing and impersonation campaigns ahead of the election. This shift underscores a move away from targeting voting infrastructure toward social engineering attacks against voters.

articles.title: NSA selects new leads for key cybersecurity posts
articles.summary: The NSA has appointed David Imbordino as the chief of its cybersecurity directorate and Bruce Jones as the head of its Cybersecurity Collaboration Center. These leadership changes involve key officials overseeing the agency's defensive and collaborative cybersecurity operations.

articles.title: Dashlane password manager users locked out by brute force attacks
articles.summary: Dashlane users are experiencing account lockouts due to widespread brute-force attacks originating from unauthorized locations and devices. The attacks appear to be targeting account credentials, triggering security protocols that restrict user access.

articles.title: USPS moving forward with mail-in ballot changes as courts weigh Trump’s election order
articles.summary: The USPS is proceeding with mail-in ballot process changes while legal challenges regarding election orders remain ongoing. The courts have currently dismissed the lawsuit as premature, but indicated that future postal regulations could create grounds for further litigation.

articles.title: What One Predator Case Can Reveal About an Online Platform’s Safety Gaps
articles.summary: This article examines how individual predator cases serve as case studies to identify and address systemic safety vulnerabilities within online platforms. It highlights the importance of analyzing exploitation methods to improve child protection measures.

articles.title: Miasma Supply Chain Attack Compromises Red Hat npm Packages with Credential-Stealing Worm
articles.summary: The Miasma supply chain attack targets Red Hat npm packages to distribute a self-propagating worm that harvests developer credentials and secrets. The campaign utilizes install-time execution and CI/CD targeting to compromise environments.

articles.title: OpenAI requires stronger authentication for users of its most powerful AI models
articles.summary: OpenAI is mandating the use of passkeys for users in its Trusted Access for Cyber (TAC) program to enhance security for its most advanced AI models starting June 1, 2026. This move highlights a push toward stronger, phishing-resistant authentication methods in the AI sector.

articles.title: WordPress malware campaign hides payloads in Steam profiles
articles.summary: A malware campaign has compromised nearly 2,000 WordPress sites by leveraging Steam Community profile comments to store command-and-control data. This technique allows attackers to mask their malicious activity by using legitimate platforms as an infrastructure for command delivery.

articles.title: Meta tries to get ahead of scammers before the World Cup begins
articles.summary: Meta is proactively addressing potential scam campaigns, including ticket fraud and credential harvesting, ahead of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. This follows FBI warnings regarding cybercriminals spoofing official tournament portals to target traveling football fans.

articles.title: NetQuest expands NetworkLens to detect threats hidden in network management traffic
articles.summary: NetQuest has expanded its NetworkLens platform to provide granular telemetry data on network management traffic, aimed at improving the accuracy of AI-driven threat detection. This update helps security teams identify malicious activity concealed within critical infrastructure management protocols.

articles.title: RaccoonLine Publishes 2026 dVPN Buyer’s Guide for Privacy-Focused Users
articles.summary: RaccoonLine has released a 2026 buyer's guide for decentralized VPNs (dVPNs), targeting privacy-conscious users seeking secure connectivity options.

articles.title: Microsoft investigates Office Apps, Teams file access issues
articles.summary: Microsoft is investigating a service outage that is preventing users from accessing files within Microsoft Teams and Office for the web. The incident is currently disrupting collaboration and document productivity across the platforms.

articles.title: Windows Netlogon RCE exploited, domain controllers at risk (CVE-2026-41089)
articles.summary: A critical stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Windows Netlogon service (CVE-2026-41089) is being actively exploited in the wild, posing a significant risk to domain controllers. Attackers can leverage this flaw to achieve remote code execution by sending specially crafted network requests to affected servers.

articles.title: GTA cheat service Atlas Menu hacked as attacker alleges screenshot spying
articles.summary: The GTA cheat service Atlas Menu suffered a significant data breach, resulting in 64,000 user records being leaked on GitHub by an attacker who claimed to have compromised the service's entire infrastructure and implemented screenshot surveillance. This incident exposes users of the cheat tool to potential credential theft and privacy violations.

articles.title: Race Against Time: Why Faster Vulnerability Alerts Matter
articles.summary: The increasing speed at which attackers exploit vulnerabilities necessitates faster alerting systems for organizations to effectively patch and reduce security exposure. Implementing rapid vulnerability notifications is essential for improving response times against modern cyber threats.

articles.title: ⚡ Weekly Recap: New Linux Flaw, PAN-OS Exploit, AI-Powered Attacks, OAuth Phishing and More
articles.summary: The weekly recap covers a range of cybersecurity threats including a new Linux vulnerability, active exploitation of PAN-OS, and the rise of AI-powered phishing and developer tool attacks. The report emphasizes a persistent and varied threat landscape requiring immediate attention to patching and security hygiene.

articles.title: Ransomware Operators Keep Business Hours. The Data Proves It
articles.summary: Data analysis of 16,699 ransomware leak-site posts reveals that threat actors predominantly operate during standard European business hours, showing a significant drop in activity on weekends. This suggests that ransomware groups function like traditional organizations with predictable, scheduled work hours.

articles.title: Secure Code Warrior connects developer training to AI usage and code risks
articles.summary: Secure Code Warrior has launched Adaptive Learning to mitigate AI-driven security risks by providing developers with contextual microlearning based on real-time code analysis. The platform aims to address the rapid increase in code churn caused by AI-assisted and autonomous development tools.

articles.title: Brute-force attack triggers Dashlane account lockouts
articles.summary: Password manager Dashlane experienced a series of brute-force attacks that resulted in temporary account lockouts for users. The company confirmed these suspensions were an automated security measure triggered by unauthorized login attempts.

articles.title: Insight bundles exposure management, patch operations, and XDR into one service
articles.summary: Insight has launched a new managed service, Insight Managed Exposure Defense, which integrates exposure management, patch operations, and XDR into a single offering to help organizations address vulnerabilities faster. The service aims to mitigate the risks posed by the rapidly shrinking window between exploit development and potential attacks.

articles.title: How to Get a Reddit API Key in 2026: Step-by-Step Guide
articles.summary: This guide provides instructions on how to obtain a Reddit API key through their official developer portal. It serves as a technical resource for developers seeking to integrate with the platform's services.

articles.title: Zero-Click pretalx XSS Flaw Lets Hackers Hijack Conference Organizer Accounts
articles.summary: A zero-click XSS vulnerability in the pretalx conference management system allows attackers to hijack organizer accounts, leading to unauthorized actions like modifying talk sessions and account permissions. The issue has been addressed in version 2026.1.0.

articles.title: Critical Windows Netlogon RCE flaw now exploited in attacks
articles.summary: The Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium has confirmed that threat actors are actively exploiting a critical, recently patched remote code execution vulnerability in the Windows Netlogon protocol.

articles.title: Palo Alto VPN bug graduates from advisory to active exploitation
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks has confirmed active exploitation of an authentication bypass vulnerability in PAN-OS, necessitating immediate emergency patching for affected users. Security researchers at Rapid7 report that attackers are actively leveraging this flaw in the wild.

articles.title: Microsoft says it will not pursue security researchers after zero-day backlash
articles.summary: Microsoft has officially stated that it will not initiate legal action against security researchers who identify and publish findings on zero-day vulnerabilities following public backlash. This policy shift aims to improve transparency and collaboration with the cybersecurity research community.

articles.title: How to Get the Most From Your Explainer Video Production Services
articles.summary: This article discusses best practices for leveraging explainer video production services to improve sales and communication efficiency. It is unrelated to cybersecurity threats or vulnerabilities.

articles.title: Webinar tomorrow: From alert to resolution in network incident response
articles.summary: This webinar highlights how IT teams can utilize automation and AI-driven workflows to reduce delays in the network incident response lifecycle. It focuses on accelerating the time from initial detection to final resolution.

articles.title: China-Aligned Groups Ramp Up Attacks: Dragon Weave Hits Czech Republic & Taiwan
articles.summary: The China-aligned threat group Dragon Weave is conducting a cyber espionage campaign against government and private sectors in the Czech Republic and Taiwan using spear-phishing to deploy the AdaptixC2 agent.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes outage affecting MFA setup, MySignIn service
articles.summary: Microsoft is addressing a service disruption that is preventing users from configuring multi-factor authentication and accessing the My Sign-Ins platform.

articles.title: Microsoft confirms outage affecting MFA, My Sign-Ins platform
articles.summary: Microsoft is investigating a service outage preventing users from configuring multi-factor authentication and accessing the My Sign-Ins platform. The issue impacts authentication security management for affected customers.

articles.title: CVE-2026-8732: The WP Maps Pro Flaw That Lets Anyone Create a WordPress Admin Without a Password
articles.summary: CVE-2026-8732 is a critical vulnerability in the WP Maps Pro WordPress plugin that allows unauthenticated attackers to create unauthorized administrative accounts. The flaw is currently being exploited in the wild, with thousands of attacks blocked within a 24-hour period.

articles.title: The Security Growth Platform: Why MSPs Are Moving Beyond vCISO Tools
articles.summary: Managed Service Providers are evolving beyond simple vCISO tools toward 'Security Growth Platforms' to better address the complex needs of modern cybersecurity practices. This shift reflects a move from basic compliance and reporting toward more comprehensive operational security management.

articles.title: Password manager Dashlane suspends customer accounts amid brute-force attacks
articles.summary: Dashlane has suspended a subset of customer accounts as a precautionary measure to counter an ongoing wave of credential stuffing and brute-force attacks. The company's automated security protocols were triggered to prevent unauthorized access while engineers work to mitigate the threat.

articles.title: Microsoft fixes KB5089549 Windows security update install issues
articles.summary: Microsoft has fixed an installation error causing 0x800f0922 issues for the KB5089549 Windows 11 security update.

articles.title: Putin sends submarines to survey Britain's subsea cables. UK deploys Royal Navy, mobilizes parliamentary draftsmen
articles.summary: The UK is deploying the Royal Navy and drafting new legislation to penalize the reckless damaging of subsea cables following reports of Russian submarine surveillance. The proposed laws introduce potential prison sentences and fines to deter interference with critical infrastructure.

articles.title: Fake Purchase Order Emails Spread Fileless PureLogs Malware via RAR Archives
articles.summary: Attackers are distributing PureLogs malware through fake purchase order emails, utilizing process hollowing and fileless execution to steal sensitive data from browsers, cryptocurrency wallets, and Discord. The malware leverages malicious RAR archives to evade detection while harvesting information from compromised Windows systems.

articles.title: Dragos acquires Phosphorus to secure extended operational technology
articles.summary: Dragos has acquired Phosphorus to expand its operational technology security platform, aiming to protect the growing number of connected devices and digital systems within critical infrastructure. This acquisition integrates Phosphorus's capabilities to secure diverse, non-traditional assets across modern operational environments.

articles.title: Election threats are focused on campaign systems, not voting machines
articles.summary: Cybersecurity researchers observe that election-related threats are increasingly targeting campaign infrastructure and utilizing AI-generated misinformation rather than physical voting machines. This shift presents a growing challenge as the public struggles to keep pace with these evolving digital risks.

articles.title: CIFSwitch, a Linux Root Bug Hidden in Plain Sight for 19 Years
articles.summary: Researchers discovered CIFSwitch, a 19-year-old privilege escalation vulnerability in Linux that allows attackers to gain root access by forging CIFS authentication keys. The bug affects several major distributions and was identified using AI-driven code analysis.

articles.title: Hackers are exploiting Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN authentication bypass (CVE-2026-0257)
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks has confirmed limited exploitation of a critical authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-0257) affecting its GlobalProtect VPN, involving the use of forged cookies. While researchers have observed successful exploitation attempts, there is currently no evidence of lateral movement within affected environments.

articles.title: OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens Stolen in codexui-android npm Supply Chain Attack
articles.summary: A malicious npm package named codexui-android, posing as a legitimate OpenAI Codex interface, has been identified for stealing developer authentication tokens. The package continues to remain available for download despite the ongoing supply chain attack.

articles.title: Critical WP Maps Pro Flaw Actively Exploited to Create Admin Accounts
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in the WP Maps Pro WordPress plugin is being actively exploited by threat actors to create unauthorized administrator accounts on affected websites. The plugin, which has over 15,000 sales, poses a significant risk to site security.

articles.title: NVIDIA goes open source with a big batch of physical AI agent tools
articles.summary: NVIDIA has released an open-source toolkit designed to simplify the development of physical AI agents for robotics, autonomous vehicles, and industrial digital twins. This initiative aims to streamline complex automation tasks by providing modular skills for AI agent deployment.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has added the Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS vulnerability CVE-2026-0257, which carries a CVSS score of 7.8, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to active exploitation. Users are urged to patch their systems to mitigate potential security risks.

articles.title: DNS-AID lets AI agents find and verify each other through DNS
articles.summary: The Linux Foundation's DNS-AID project leverages the Domain Name System to provide a vendor-neutral directory for AI agents and servers to discover and authenticate one another. This initiative aims to streamline secure communication between disparate AI systems across multiple platforms.

articles.title: Asimily turns device risk into automated network policy
articles.summary: Asimily has launched a new 'Segmentation Orchestration' platform that integrates device risk intelligence with automated network policy enforcement to defend connected devices. The tool aims to close security gaps by streamlining the transition from asset visibility and vulnerability prioritization to actionable network segmentation.

articles.title: The Pentagon Finally Admits That Location Data Is a Battlefield Problem
articles.summary: The Pentagon has officially acknowledged that commercially available location data poses a significant security risk by allowing adversaries to track U.S. military personnel. This confirms long-standing warnings that ad-tech networks function as a form of accessible surveillance infrastructure.

articles.title: Data discovery gaps that catch enterprises off guard
articles.summary: Avani Desai of Schellman discusses the critical discrepancy between perceived data awareness and the reality of shadow data discovered during security audits. The interview highlights common risks such as abandoned cloud storage and the challenges of managing data post-merger.

articles.title: EU organizations buckle under rising compliance pressure
articles.summary: EU organizations are facing significant operational strain as they adapt to evolving cybersecurity regulations like NIS2 and DORA. The complexity of these frameworks, combined with emerging AI security challenges, is creating a state of compliance overload.

articles.title: Governing shadow AI without killing innovation
articles.summary: Alan Snyder of NowSecure discusses the challenge of balancing the rapid adoption of shadow AI with necessary security governance. He emphasizes that organizations must integrate risk management strategies to keep pace with innovation while defending against emerging threats.

articles.title: 145 AI laws passed in 2025 and privacy teams aren’t catching a break
articles.summary: In 2025, 145 new AI laws were enacted alongside widespread shadow AI risks, where over 60% of business software providers failed to disclose third-party AI subprocessors. This regulatory surge and lack of transparency significantly increase the operational and compliance burden on privacy teams.

articles.title: Afghan finance officials targeted by suspected Pakistani cyberespionage campaign
articles.summary: A suspected Pakistan-linked hacking group has initiated a cyberespionage campaign targeting Afghanistan's Ministry of Finance and various provincial government officials. The operation appears to be focused on intelligence gathering within the Afghan government infrastructure.

articles.title: Unknown hacker group targeted Russian maritime universities, diplomats for nearly two years
articles.summary: An unidentified threat actor has conducted a two-year espionage campaign targeting Russian maritime universities and diplomatic entities. The attacks primarily focused on educational institutions training personnel for the Russian shipping and fishing sectors.

articles.title: CVE-2026-0257: Rapid7 Caught Attackers Abusing Forged VPN Cookies Against Multiple Customers
articles.summary: Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-0257, a vulnerability in Palo Alto GlobalProtect that allows for VPN authentication bypass via forged cookies. Rapid7 reported confirmed compromises across multiple customer environments following the release of a patch.

articles.title: 27,000-Download Codex UI Tool Secretly Stole OpenAI Refresh Tokens
articles.summary: A malicious npm package named Codex UI, which received 27,000 weekly downloads, was discovered exfiltrating OpenAI refresh tokens from developer environments. This incident poses a significant threat to affected users by enabling potential unauthorized account access.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 99
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights recent malware campaigns, including Ghost CMS being compromised via CVE-2026-26980 for ClickFix attacks, a widespread supply chain attack on package managers, and new insights into the Lazarus group's RemotePE RAT.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 579 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: The latest edition of the Security Affairs newsletter covers a significant data leak involving 5 million Charter Communications customers by the ShinyHunters group and a targeted phishing campaign against journalists. These reports highlight ongoing risks to large-scale data privacy and media professionals.

articles.title: WP Maps Pro bug exploited to create admin accounts on WordPress sites
articles.summary: A vulnerability in the WP Maps Pro WordPress plugin is being exploited by attackers to create unauthorized administrative accounts on target websites. This security flaw allows unauthenticated users to gain full control over affected installations.

articles.title: Dutch Authorities Dismantle Botnet Linked to 17 Million Infected Devices
articles.summary: Dutch authorities successfully dismantled a massive botnet consisting of 17 million infected devices, including smartphones and IoT hardware, that were used for malicious cyberattacks. The operation involved seizing over 200 servers in the Netherlands to neutralize the infrastructure.

articles.title: Week in review: Infostealer dropped via FortiClient EMS flaw, exploited Trend Micro Apex One flaw
articles.summary: Recent cybersecurity reports highlight the exploitation of vulnerabilities in FortiClient EMS and Trend Micro Apex One to deploy infostealers. Additionally, the update discusses the escalating security challenges facing crypto payment firms under pressure from advanced persistent threats.

articles.title: Palo Alto GlobalProtect VPN auth bypass flaw now exploited in attacks
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks has confirmed that the CVE-2026-0257 authentication bypass vulnerability in PAN-OS GlobalProtect is currently being exploited by attackers to compromise corporate networks.

articles.title: Fake Anthropic Sites Deliver Fileless Infostealer to Claude Code Users
articles.summary: Threat actors are distributing a fileless infostealer through deceptive websites impersonating Anthropic to compromise the credentials of Claude Code users. This campaign leverages stealthy techniques to evade detection while targeting sensitive browser data.

articles.title: ShinyHunters Leaks Charter Communications Data, Potentially Impacting 5 Million Customers
articles.summary: The ShinyHunters cybercrime group leaked records of approximately 5 million Charter Communications customers after the company refused to pay a ransom demand. This incident follows an extortion attempt by the threat actors targeting the major U.S. telecommunications firm.

articles.title: New CIFSwitch Linux flaw gives root on multiple distributions
articles.summary: A newly identified local privilege escalation vulnerability called 'CIFSwitch' affects the Linux kernel, enabling attackers to gain root access by exploiting the CIFS authentication key mechanism.

articles.title: Signal Phishing Campaign Targets Journalists and Activists to Steal Backup Recovery Keys
articles.summary: A targeted phishing campaign is impersonating Signal Support via SMS to trick users into revealing their backup recovery keys, allowing attackers to decrypt their entire message history. This sophisticated social engineering attack specifically threatens the privacy of journalists and activists.

articles.title: Botnet of 17 Million Devices Dismantled in the Netherlands
articles.summary: Dutch authorities successfully dismantled a massive botnet comprising 17 million infected devices by seizing 200 servers associated with the proxy service Asocks. The operation targeted a widespread network of compromised computers, tablets, and smartphones used for illicit activities.

articles.title: Botnet of 17 Million Devices Dismantled in the Netherlands
articles.summary: Dutch authorities successfully dismantled a massive botnet comprising 17 million infected devices by seizing over 200 servers linked to the Asocks proxy service. The operation aimed to disrupt the infrastructure used for cybercriminal activities across global endpoints.

articles.title: PAN-OS GlobalProtect Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-0257) Under Active Exploitation
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks has confirmed active exploitation of CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass vulnerability affecting PAN-OS and Prisma Access that allows unauthorized VPN access.

articles.title: Lone attacker published 14 malicious npm packages mimicking popular OpenSearch, Elasticsearch libraries
articles.summary: A lone threat actor deployed 14 malicious npm packages designed to impersonate popular OpenSearch and Elasticsearch libraries. Microsoft successfully identified and removed the packages from the registry before widespread impact occurred.

articles.title: ICE to keep an eye on your eyes under $25M biometric scanner deal
articles.summary: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has secured a $25 million contract for advanced biometric eye-scanning technology to enhance identity verification processes. This move raises significant privacy concerns regarding government surveillance and the collection of sensitive biometric data.

articles.title: No fix yet for critical RCE bug in open-source Git service Gogs - exploit module is out
articles.summary: A critical remote code execution vulnerability in the open-source Gogs service remains unpatched despite being reported months ago, and a functional exploit module is now publicly available.

articles.title: Meet GREYVIBE, the Russia-Linked Hacking Group Using AI to Target Ukraine and Still Making Rookie Mistakes
articles.summary: The newly identified Russia-linked threat actor GREYVIBE is actively targeting Ukrainian government and military organizations using AI-assisted malware. Despite their advanced tools, researchers have observed the group committing significant operational security errors.

articles.title: ChatGPT share links abused to host fake outage pages to deliver malware
articles.summary: Threat actors are exploiting the ChatGPT share feature to redirect users to fraudulent outage pages that distribute malware disguised as the official desktop application. This technique leverages the trust associated with OpenAI's platform to deceive victims into downloading malicious files.

articles.title: Tennessee man linked to 764 accused of series of crimes against children dating back to 2022
articles.summary: Zachary Sweeney, a Tennessee man linked to a child exploitation network, has been charged with a series of crimes against minors across multiple states following an FBI investigation. The individual allegedly traveled across state lines to harm victims starting as early as 2022.

articles.title: California AG sues 23andMe over 2023 breach exposing health data
articles.summary: The California Attorney General has filed a lawsuit against 23andMe for failing to adequately protect the sensitive genetic and personal data of its customers during a 2023 security breach.

articles.title: ChatGPhish Vulnerability Turns ChatGPT Web Summaries Into a Phishing Surface
articles.summary: Researchers identified a vulnerability dubbed ChatGPhish in ChatGPT that exploits trust in Markdown formatting to facilitate phishing attacks via prompt injection. The flaw allows attackers to manipulate AI-generated content to direct users to malicious links.

articles.title: 23andMe inherits lawsuit over 'disturbing' DNA data breach
articles.summary: 23andMe is facing a lawsuit from the California Attorney General for allegedly downplaying the severity of a 2023 massive DNA data breach. The complaint highlights failures in cybersecurity disclosures and incident response practices.

articles.title: Federal audit reveals NIST’s NVD is plagued by poor planning and duplication
articles.summary: A Commerce Inspector General audit found that the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD) suffers from significant mismanagement, including a backlog of 27,000 unprocessed vulnerabilities and inefficient duplication of efforts with CISA.

articles.title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit
articles.summary: Threat actors are leveraging LLM agents to perform post-exploitation activities after gaining initial access to Marimo network notebooks via the CVE-2026-39987 vulnerability. The attackers successfully extracted cloud credentials following the system compromise.

articles.title: From $5 Attacks to Botnet-Powered Platforms: Inside the DDoS-as-a- Service Market
articles.summary: The DDoS-as-a-Service market has matured into a professionalized ecosystem featuring subscription models, support services, and reseller programs that lower the barrier to entry for launching attacks. This evolution highlights a significant shift toward accessible, commercialized cybercrime infrastructure.

articles.title: Dutch govt disrupts malware botnet with 17 million infected devices
articles.summary: Dutch authorities successfully dismantled a massive botnet consisting of 17 million infected devices and seized over 200 associated servers. This operation marks a significant blow to the infrastructure supporting the malicious network.

articles.title: Dutch police disrupts botnet composed of 17 million devices
articles.summary: Dutch law enforcement dismantled a massive botnet consisting of 17 million infected devices by seizing 200 command-and-control servers. The operation was initiated following a security researcher's report to the National Cyber Security Center.

articles.title: Microsoft calls zero-day releases ‘never justifiable’ as researcher threatens to drop more
articles.summary: Microsoft has condemned the practice of releasing zero-day vulnerabilities with proof-of-concept code on GitHub, labeling it unjustifiable as a researcher threatens to disclose more flaws. This action increases immediate risk by providing attackers with ready-to-use exploit material.

articles.title: Dutch cops wrest 17M devices from mystery botnet's clutches
articles.summary: Dutch law enforcement dismantled a massive botnet by seizing control of 200 servers hosted within the Netherlands. This operation effectively neutralized 17 million compromised devices globally.

articles.title: Google Chrome adds session cookie theft protection for all users
articles.summary: Google has launched Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) for Chrome to protect users against account hijacking by tying session cookies to specific hardware. This feature aims to neutralize session cookie theft, a common method used by infostealer malware.

articles.title: ChatGPT blindly trusts browser content, turning the page into a payload
articles.summary: Researchers have discovered that ChatGPT can be manipulated into executing malicious code by processing untrusted content from web pages, turning the browser into an attack vector. This vulnerability highlights potential risks in AI-integrated browsing tools when handling external data.

articles.title: Russia-linked threat group put ChatGPT to work from lure to payload
articles.summary: The Russia-linked threat actor GREYVIBE utilized AI-driven tools, including ChatGPT, to streamline their malicious operations, ranging from social engineering lures to the deployment of payloads against Ukrainian government and military entities.

articles.title: New infostealer reaches enterprise devices through FortiClient EMS vulnerability
articles.summary: Attackers are exploiting a known improper access control vulnerability (CVE-2026-35616) in FortiClient EMS to deliver infostealer malware by masquerading as legitimate endpoint updates. The campaign leverages managed VPN scripting workflows to compromise enterprise devices.

articles.title: New Russian-Linked GREYVIBE Targets Ukraine with AI-Powered Cyberattacks
articles.summary: A newly identified, Russian-linked threat actor known as GREYVIBE has been launching persistent cyberattacks against Ukrainian entities since August 2025. The group utilizes AI-powered tools and aligns its operations with Russian state interests.

articles.title: DIL Observatory: when the World Escalates, the Underground Responds
articles.summary: Digital Intelligence Lab has launched an observatory to track and analyze the correlation between global geopolitical events and cyber activity. The initiative aims to provide insights into how real-world instability manifests as traceable patterns in the cyber threat landscape.

articles.title: Man sent to prison for selling data of 7 millions elderly Americans

articles.summary: The hacking group ShinyHunters has leaked the personal information of 4.9 million Charter Communications customers, including names, addresses, and contact details. articles.title: US charges Google security engineer with Polymarket insider trading
articles.summary: A Google security engineer has been charged with insider trading for allegedly using confidential company data to win $1.2 million in bets on the Polymarket prediction platform. The case highlights the misuse of privileged corporate access for personal financial gain.

articles.title: LinkedIn-themed phishing abuses Adobe’s A/B testing platform
articles.summary: A sophisticated phishing campaign is targeting professionals by using fake LinkedIn-themed business inquiries that leverage Adobe's legitimate A/B testing platform to bypass security filters. articles.title: The Deliverability Problem: How New Platforms Are Solving Inbox Placement
articles.summary: This article discusses the technical challenges of email deliverability and how emerging platforms are improving inbox placement rates for digital communications.

articles.title: BTMOB RAT Gives Criminals a Point-and-Click Kit to Take Over Your Android Phone
articles.summary: BTMOB is a new Android Remote Access Trojan (RAT) sold as an easy-to-use kit that allows non-technical criminals to perform full-device takeovers and data theft. By offering a built-in APK builder for a one-time fee, it significantly lowers the barrier to entry for mobile cyberattacks.

articles.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 4.8, prepares Mythos-class models for all customers
articles.summary: Anthropic has released the Claude Opus 4.8 model, focusing on improved output honesty, and announced plans to expand access to its Mythos-class models to all customers.

articles.title: Netskope extends data localization capabilities with NewEdge updates
articles.summary: Netskope has expanded its NewEdge network infrastructure to provide enhanced data localization and sovereignty capabilities across more global regions. This update aims to assist organizations in meeting stringent compliance and data governance requirements for network transport and processing.

articles.title: Claroty targets cyber-physical system risks with AI-powered security agent
articles.summary: Claroty has introduced an AI-powered security agent called Claroty Claire, specifically designed to protect mission-critical cyber-physical systems by leveraging a specialized language model. The tool aims to improve the safety and uptime of infrastructure against an evolving threat landscape.

articles.title: Humanix expands detection to identify live violations of security procedures
articles.summary: Humanix has launched a new capability to detect real-time violations of identity verification procedures within IT support workflows to prevent social engineering-based unauthorized access. This tool aims to protect help desk agents from manipulation tactics used by attackers to bypass security safeguards during credential resets.

articles.title: Kimsuky Deploys HTTPSpy, Expands Arsenal with HelloDoor and VS Code Tunnels
articles.summary: The North Korean threat actor Kimsuky is targeting South Korean organizations using new malware variants like HTTPSpy and HelloDoor, alongside social engineering tactics. These attacks utilize sophisticated lures such as fake security and Webex portals to compromise military and corporate entities.

articles.title: The behavioral signals that sharpen Trojan malware detection
articles.summary: A recent study highlights the importance of effective feature selection from sandbox behavioral data to improve the detection accuracy of Trojan malware. By filtering out irrelevant noise from sandbox telemetry, security analysts can significantly enhance the performance of threat detection models.

articles.title: Product showcase: TotalAV helps iOS users clean up their digital mess
articles.summary: TotalAV has released a mobile security suite for iOS and other platforms designed to protect users against malicious sites, SMS scams, and credential exposure. The app features a Smart Scan tool to audit device settings and browser security for improved digital hygiene.

articles.title: New infosec products of the month: May 2026
articles.summary: This article highlights recent product launches in the cybersecurity industry for May 2026, including a focus on Operant AI's new endpoint protection tool for AI agents. The list covers updates from various vendors aiming to address emerging enterprise security needs.

articles.summary: Anthropic is preparing to release its advanced Mythos-class AI models to the public following a delay intended to mitigate potential software security risks.

articles.title: GreyVibe hackers use ChatGPT, Gemini to power cyberattacks
articles.summary: The Russian-linked threat group GreyVibe is utilizing AI chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini to craft deceptive lures for cyberattacks against Ukrainian entities. This activity highlights the emerging trend of state-sponsored actors integrating generative AI to enhance their offensive capabilities.

articles.title: Troops’ phones gave away location data to foreign adversaries
articles.summary: Foreign adversaries have been exploiting commercial location tracking data from the smartphones of military personnel to pinpoint their positions. Consequently, lawmakers are urging the Department of Defense to implement stricter security controls regarding mobile device usage.

articles.title: BTMOB Android malware service generates custom phishing payloads
articles.summary: BTMOB is a new Android remote access trojan that provides cybercriminals with a builder interface to create customized phishing payloads. This service lowers the barrier for attackers to deploy targeted mobile malware.

articles.title: Disgruntled 0-day hunter 'humiliated' by Microsoft pledges 'bone shattering drop' as Redmond calls cops
articles.summary: A disgruntled security researcher who claims to possess several zero-day vulnerabilities, including some under active exploitation, has threatened to release them publicly after Microsoft involved law enforcement. The researcher intends to potentially dump these exploits on July 14.

articles.title: Snowflake buys Natoma to help freeze out rogue agents
articles.summary: Snowflake has acquired the company Natoma, marking its sixth acquisition since June 2025 as part of an effort to enhance security against malicious actors. This move reflects the company's ongoing strategy to bolster its database protection capabilities.

articles.title: Carnival Data Breach Exposes Personal Data of Nearly 6 Million Customers
articles.summary: Carnival Corporation disclosed a data breach resulting from a social engineering attack that compromised employee accounts, exposing the personal information of nearly 6 million customers. The company is currently in the process of notifying all affected individuals.

articles.title: FBI warns of fake FIFA websites running World Cup fraud schemes
articles.summary: The FBI has issued an alert regarding fraudulent websites impersonating FIFA to steal financial data and distribute fake World Cup tickets. These schemes leverage the upcoming 2026 event to target unsuspecting fans through phishing and illicit sales.

articles.title: House panel poised to hold hearing centered on AI impact on cyber
articles.summary: The House Homeland Security Committee is scheduled to host a public hearing to examine the impact of artificial intelligence on cybersecurity. This event is part of an ongoing series of congressional reviews regarding emerging tech threats.

articles.title: Google security engineer accused of turning confidential search trends into $1.2M win on Polymarket
articles.summary: A Google security engineer has been accused of leveraging unauthorized access to confidential internal search trend data to execute profitable trades on the prediction market Polymarket. The individual allegedly generated $1.2 million in illicit gains using nonpublic information.

articles.title: Hackers exploit FortiClient EMS flaw to push infostealer malware
articles.summary: Hackers are actively exploiting an authentication bypass vulnerability in FortiClient EMS to distribute a new credential-stealing malware known as EKZ. The campaign leverages CVE-2026-35616 to compromise enterprise management servers.

articles.title: Critical Gogs RCE Vulnerability Lets Any Authenticated User Execute Arbitrary Code
articles.summary: A critical RCE vulnerability in Gogs, rated 9.4 on the CVSS scale, allows authenticated users to execute arbitrary code on affected servers. The flaw currently lacks an official CVE identifier.

articles.title: The CISO Whisperer’s Watch List For The Gartner Security & Risk Management Summit 2026
articles.summary: This article highlights key focus areas and recommendations for CISOs attending the upcoming 2026 Gartner Security & Risk Management Summit. It serves as a strategic guide for industry leaders navigating the evolving threat landscape.

articles.title: Microsoft tests the 15-character limit of Windows Server admins' patience
articles.summary: Microsoft's May security update introduced a bug that causes issues for Windows Server hostnames exactly 15 characters long. This flaw disrupts system operations for administrators using specific naming conventions.

articles.title: CVE-2026-35616: FortiClient EMS Flaw Actively Exploited in Malware Attacks
articles.summary: FortiClient EMS is currently being targeted by threat actors exploiting a critical, unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability (CVE-2026-35616) to deploy information-stealing malware. Security teams are urged to ensure systems are patched against this high-severity flaw.

articles.title: Resecurity Supports Microsoft DCU in Disrupting Fox Tempest ’s Cybercriminal Code-Signing Ecosystem
articles.summary: Resecurity assisted Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit in disrupting Fox Tempest, a malware-signing-as-a-service operation that utilized fraudulent certificates to legitimize malicious software.

articles.title: Threat Actors Exploit Critical FortiClient EMS Flaw to Deploy Credential Stealer
articles.summary: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical vulnerability in FortiClient Endpoint Management Server (EMS) to distribute credential-stealing malware across managed endpoints. Although a patch is available, attackers are leveraging the infrastructure to masquerade malicious payloads as legitimate Fortinet updates.

articles.title: IBM and Red Hat are betting $5 billion that open source needs a security guard
articles.summary: IBM and Red Hat have launched Project Lightwell, a $5 billion initiative utilizing AI and a dedicated engineering workforce to identify and remediate security vulnerabilities within open source software for enterprise environments.

articles.title: New Gogs zero-day flaw lets hackers get remote code execution
articles.summary: An unpatched zero-day vulnerability in Gogs self-hosted Git services exposes internet-facing instances to remote code execution attacks. This flaw allows unauthorized actors to execute arbitrary commands, posing a significant security risk.

articles.title: Cybercriminals sail away with data from 6 million Carnival customers
articles.summary: Carnival Corporation confirmed a data breach affecting 6 million customers after a phishing attack allowed unauthorized access to an employee's account. The ShinyHunters hacking group claimed responsibility for the incident.

articles.title: How SIEM helps MSPs reduce noise and stop threats faster
articles.summary: This article explores how SIEM solutions assist Managed Service Providers (MSPs) in managing alert fatigue by filtering noise and increasing visibility to accelerate threat response.

articles.title: Cruise giant Carnival confirms data breach affecting nearly 6 million people
articles.summary: Carnival Corporation disclosed a data breach involving unauthorized access to an employee account, resulting in the theft of personal information for approximately 6 million individuals. The incident occurred after attackers compromised internal systems in April.

articles.title: Microsoft Slams Public Zero-Day Disclosures Amid GitHub Researcher Account Removal
articles.summary: Microsoft is advocating for Coordinated Vulnerability Disclosure (CVD) following the unauthorized public release of zero-day vulnerabilities by a security researcher. articles.title: Microsoft’s Copilot trust test: Zero findings, more models, wider oversight
articles.summary: Microsoft 365 Copilot has successfully achieved recertification under the ISO/IEC 42001:2023 standard for AI management systems for the second consecutive year with zero non-conformities. The certification validates Microsoft's adherence to rigorous frameworks regarding AI governance, data management, and human oversight.

articles.title: Canadian man gets 33 years for using social media to coerce US children into sending sexual content
articles.summary: A Canadian man was sentenced to 33 years in prison for using fraudulent social media profiles to coerce American minors into sharing sexually explicit materials. The case highlights the severe consequences for individuals engaging in the sexual exploitation of children through online manipulation.

articles.title: ThreatsDay Bulletin: Claude Security Plugin, Azure Priv-Esc, Kali365 MFA Bypass, FIFA Scams +15 More
articles.summary: This bulletin covers a diverse range of current cyber threats, including newly discovered vulnerabilities in Azure, bypasses for MFA systems, and ongoing social engineering campaigns targeting global events. articles.summary: CISA has expanded its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include multiple flaws affecting Daemon Tools, TanStack, Nx Console, Windows Shell, and ConnectWise ScreenConnect. Organizations are urged to review these additions and prioritize remediation to mitigate the risk of active exploitation.

articles.summary: Security researchers discovered a five-stage exploit chain that leveraged a series of common anti-patterns to gain unauthorized write access to Zapier's internal and public developer SDK packages. Zapier successfully mitigated the risk by revoking the exposed NPM token and tightening AWS permissions.

articles.title: Zapier fixes bug chain that researchers say risked widespread account takeover
articles.summary: Zapier has addressed a multi-step vulnerability chain that could have allowed unauthorized attackers to hijack user accounts across numerous integrated applications. The flaw, now patched, posed a significant risk of widespread account takeover.

articles.summary: The 2026 World Cup faces significant cybersecurity risks from diverse threat actors, including ransomware groups and state-aligned entities, targeting critical infrastructure. articles.title: Authorities seize 800 servers used for cyberattacks and disinformation
articles.summary: Dutch authorities arrested two men and seized 800 servers used to host cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns allegedly supporting Russian state interests. The operation targeted a hosting provider suspected of violating international sanctions laws by enabling activities aimed at destabilizing democratic and economic systems.

articles.title: FBI warns of Kali365 phishing service targeting Microsoft 365 accounts
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a warning regarding the Kali365 phishing-as-a-service platform, which targets Microsoft 365 accounts by exploiting OAuth device code authentication to steal session tokens and bypass MFA.

articles.title: Ghost CMS CVE-2026-26980 Exploited to Hijack 700+ Sites for ClickFix Attacks
articles.summary: Threat actors are exploiting a critical SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-26980) in Ghost CMS to inject malicious scripts and facilitate ClickFix attacks across over 700 websites.

articles.title: US states step up cyber defenses to protect local communities
articles.summary: U.S. state governments are actively strengthening cybersecurity for local communities by implementing shared defense programs, regional security centers, and specialized workforce initiatives. These measures aim to enhance regional resilience and reduce costs through centralized services and procurement.

articles.title: The Alert Firehose Finally Meets Its Match
articles.summary: The integration of agentic AI into Network Detection and Response (NDR) tools is successfully addressing long-standing issues with alert fatigue and false positives. This evolution allows security teams to triage incidents more efficiently and identify threats earlier in the lifecycle.

articles.title: Netherlands Busts Bulletproof Hosting Network Linked to Disinformation and Cybercrime
articles.summary: Dutch authorities dismantled a bulletproof hosting network used for cybercrime, disinformation campaigns, and bypassing Russian sanctions. Two suspects were arrested in connection with the operation.

articles.title: Zero-Click WhatsApp Account Takeover Hits iPhone Users Running iOS 16. No Linked Devices, No Warning
articles.summary: A zero-click vulnerability targeting iPhones running iOS 16 allows attackers to hijack WhatsApp accounts without user interaction or linked device notifications. This exploit facilitates unauthorized access, enabling malicious actors to send fraudulent messages from the victim's account.

articles.title: Lazarus Deploys RemotePE Memory-Only RAT Against Financial and Crypto Firms
articles.summary: The North Korean-linked Lazarus Group is utilizing a new cross-platform memory-only malware called RemotePE to target financial and cryptocurrency organizations through a multi-stage infection chain. The operation employs specialized loaders, DPAPILoader and RemotePELoader, to execute the malicious payload.

articles.title: Dutch authorities dismantle hosting network allegedly used for cyberattacks and disinformation
articles.summary: Dutch authorities arrested two individuals and seized 800 servers associated with Stark Industries, a hosting provider allegedly facilitating cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns. The operation targeted infrastructure suspected of supporting Russian interference activities.

articles.title: Anthropic to release Mythos-class models to the public
articles.summary: Anthropic is expanding access to its Mythos-class AI vulnerability-detection models to government and select users while continuing to develop safety guardrails. The company remains cautious about a full public release to prevent potential misuse of the flaw-finding capabilities.

articles.title: FBI director Kash Patel’s brand website taken offline after malware reports
articles.summary: The merchandise website for FBI Director Kash Patel was taken offline following a compromise that leveraged a fake Cloudflare prompt to execute a ClickFix malware attack on visitors.

articles.title: TrapDoor Supply Chain Attack Spreads Credential-Stealing Malware via npm, PyPI, and CratesIO
articles.summary: The TrapDoor supply chain attack campaign has compromised over 34 malicious packages across npm, PyPI, and Crates.io to distribute credential-stealing malware. This coordinated effort involves hundreds of malicious package versions impacting multiple software development ecosystems.

articles.title: Lessons for organizations from the Verizon 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report
articles.summary: This article highlights the release of the Verizon 2026 Data Breach Investigations Report (DBIR) and emphasizes its value as a essential resource for organizations to understand current security threats. It frames the report as a top-tier industry document that provides critical insights for strengthening cybersecurity posture.

articles.title: OpenHack: Open-source AI-powered vulnerability research
articles.summary: Hadrian has released OpenHack, an MIT-licensed, open-source project that utilizes AI agents to automate the vulnerability research process within developer coding harnesses. This tool packages expert-led research methodologies into a workspace compatible with existing AI coding assistants.

articles.title: Boards want cyber risk in dollars, not CVE counts
articles.summary: Security leaders are increasingly pressured to translate complex technical vulnerabilities into financial risk metrics to better communicate with corporate boards. This shift emphasizes mapping cyber threats to critical business assets to justify security investment in terms executives understand.

articles.title: Turns out the C-suite loves shadow AI
articles.summary: A TrustedTech report reveals that senior decision-makers are the primary drivers of shadow AI usage, continuing to utilize unapproved tools despite clear awareness of the associated security and privacy risks. This suggests that shadow AI adoption is a leadership-driven trend rather than a grassroots employee practice.

articles.title: Hacker Selling 340 Million OnlyFans User Records Built From Old Breaches
articles.summary: A threat actor is offering a database of 340 million OnlyFans user records for sale, reportedly aggregated by cross-referencing previous data breaches and public profile information. This incident highlights the risks of credential stuffing and data exposure through the aggregation of legacy breach data.

articles.title: Ghost CMS SQL injection flaw exploited in large-scale ClickFix campaign
articles.summary: A large-scale campaign is actively exploiting a critical SQL injection vulnerability in Ghost CMS, identified as CVE-2026-26980, to execute ClickFix malicious JavaScript attacks. The vulnerability enables attackers to inject unauthorized code, posing a significant risk to affected installations.

articles.title: SECURITY AFFAIRS MALWARE NEWSLETTER ROUND 98
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights several recent supply chain attacks and malware campaigns targeting npm packages and GitHub actions, emphasizing the growing threat to software development ecosystems. It covers incidents involving credential stealers, Shai-Hulud clones, and compromised development tools.

articles.title: Security Affairs newsletter Round 578 by Pierluigi Paganini – INTERNATIONAL EDITION
articles.summary: This newsletter highlights a critical SQL injection vulnerability in Drupal (CVE-2026-9082) that is currently being exploited in the wild, alongside discussions on extortion-based cyberattacks.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Project Glasswing: 10,000+ Vulnerabilities Found in One Month, and the Patching Problem Has Never Been More Obvious
articles.summary: Anthropic's Project Glasswing, powered by the Claude Mythos Preview, identified over 10,000 critical security vulnerabilities in its first month, highlighting a significant and growing gap in organizational patching capabilities.

articles.title: Week in review: GitHub breached via poisoned VS Code extension, critical NGINX flaw exploited
articles.summary: GitHub confirmed an internal breach caused by a malicious VS Code extension, alongside reports of active exploitation of a critical NGINX vulnerability.

articles.title: U.S. CISA adds a flaw in Drupal Core to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog
articles.summary: CISA has updated its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog to include a critical vulnerability in Drupal Core. This action mandates that federal agencies address the security flaw to mitigate potential exploitation risks.

articles.title: Laravel Lang packages hijacked to deploy credential-stealing malware
articles.summary: Attackers compromised Laravel Lang localization packages by abusing GitHub version tags to inject credential-stealing malware into Composer dependencies. This supply chain attack successfully distributed malicious code to developers utilizing the popular localization library.

articles.title: npm Adds 2FA-Gated Publishing and Package Install Controls Against Supply Chain Attacks
articles.summary: GitHub has introduced staged publishing for npm, requiring two-factor authentication (2FA) and manual approval before package releases become publicly available to mitigate supply chain attacks.

articles.title: CVE-2026-9082: Drupal’s Highly Critical SQL Injection Flaw Is Already Under Active Attack
articles.summary: A highly critical SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-9082) affecting Drupal sites using PostgreSQL is currently being exploited in the wild shortly after its patch release.

articles.title: Packagist Supply Chain Attack Infects 8 Packages Using GitHub-Hosted Linux Malware
articles.summary: A coordinated supply chain attack compromised eight Packagist packages by injecting malicious code into package.json files to execute Linux binaries from GitHub. The campaign strategically targets projects that ship both PHP and JavaScript components.

articles.title: Italy disrupts CINEMAGOAL piracy app that stole streaming auth codes
articles.summary: Italian authorities dismantled the CINEMAGOAL piracy app, which illegally accessed streaming service authentication tokens to provide unauthorized content distribution. The operation effectively neutralized a significant ecosystem facilitating large-scale digital content theft.

articles.title: Why pure extortion is replacing traditional ransomware
articles.summary: Ransomware gangs are evolving their tactics by moving away from system encryption toward pure data extortion, focusing on stealing sensitive information and threatening public leaks to exert pressure. This shift enables attackers to operate more stealthily while maintaining high leverage over their victims.

articles.title: Claude Mythos AI Finds 10,000 High-Severity Flaws in Widely Used Software
articles.summary: Anthropic's Project Glasswing initiative has utilized AI to identify over 10,000 high- or critical-severity vulnerabilities in essential global software systems within its first month of operation.

articles.title: RondoDox Botnet Exploits Critical 2018 Vulnerability to Hijack ASUS Routers
articles.summary: The RondoDox botnet is actively leveraging a critical 2018 security vulnerability to bypass authentication and compromise over a million ASUS routers. This campaign highlights the persistent risk posed by unpatched legacy vulnerabilities in network hardware.

articles.title: AI eyes scanning for bugs create a worrisome Linux security trend
articles.summary: The emergence of AI-driven vulnerability discovery tools is accelerating the identification of Linux kernel flaws, such as Dirty Frag and Copy Fail, creating new challenges for system security maintenance. This trend suggests that attackers are increasingly leveraging automated systems to find and exploit vulnerabilities at a faster pace.

articles.title: Dirty Frag, Copy Fail, Fragnesia: The start of a worrisome Linux security trend
articles.summary: The emergence of several Linux-related vulnerabilities nicknamed 'Dirty Frag,' 'Copy Fail,' and 'Fragnesia' signals a potential rise in systematic exploit discovery. The article questions whether these findings are a natural security evolution or an effect of AI-driven vulnerability scanning.

articles.title: Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised to Deliver Cross-Platform Credential Stealer
articles.summary: Malicious actors compromised several Laravel-Lang PHP packages to inject a credential-stealing framework, marking a significant software supply chain attack. Users of the affected packages are at risk of data theft via the compromised tags.

articles.title: Ghostwriter Is Back, Using a Ukrainian Learning Platform as Bait to Hit Government Targets
articles.summary: The Belarus-linked threat actor Ghostwriter has launched a new phishing campaign targeting Ukrainian government employees by spoofing the legitimate Prometheus online learning platform to deliver malware and Cobalt Strike. This resurfacing of the UAC-0057 group highlights a continued focus on critical government infrastructure.

articles.title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-48172 Exploited to Run Scripts as Root
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in the LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin (CVE-2026-48172) is being actively exploited, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary scripts with root privileges.

articles.title: Drupal Core SQL Injection Bug Actively Exploited, Added to CISA KEV
articles.summary: CISA has added a critical SQL injection vulnerability (CVE-2026-9082) in Drupal Core to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog due to reports of active exploitation. Organizations using Drupal are urged to apply the latest security patches to mitigate this risk.

articles.title: CISA to allow researchers to report vulnerabilities to exploited bugs catalog
articles.summary: CISA has introduced a new nomination process allowing security researchers and industry partners to directly report vulnerabilities for inclusion in the agency's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. This initiative aims to improve the speed and accuracy of tracking actively exploited security flaws.

articles.title: A Russian speaker and jailbroken Gemini went on a hacking spree and emptied at least one MAGA victim's crypto wallets
articles.summary: A threat actor utilized a jailbroken instance of Google's Gemini AI to facilitate a hacking spree that resulted in the theft of cryptocurrency from targeted victims. The incident highlights the growing risk of adversarial AI being leveraged to assist in malicious cyber activities.

articles.title: FBI warns about fast-growing phishing kit targeting Microsoft 365 users
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a warning regarding Kali365, a phishing kit that exploits Microsoft's legitimate device authorization process to gain persistent, unauthorized access to user accounts. This tool has seen rapid adoption by cybercriminals since its emergence in April.

articles.title: FBI warns of Kali365 phishing-as-a-service after April Microsoft 365 attacks
articles.summary: The FBI has issued an advisory regarding Kali365, a Telegram-based phishing-as-a-service platform used to harvest OAuth tokens for compromising Microsoft 365 environments. The alert follows a series of targeted attacks observed in April.

articles.title: FBI Warns of Kali365 Phishing Service Targeting Microsoft 365 Account
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a warning regarding Kali365, a phishing-as-a-service platform that enables attackers to bypass multi-factor authentication and compromise Microsoft 365 accounts. This tool simplifies account hijacking by eliminating the need for password-based credentials.

articles.title: Meta settles school district lawsuit claiming addictive design harmed students' mental health
articles.summary: Meta has reached a settlement in the first of over 1,200 lawsuits filed by school districts alleging that the company's social media platforms are designed to be addictive and harmful to student mental health.

articles.title: Megalodon chums the waters in 5.5K+ GitHub repo poisonings
articles.summary: The 'Megalodon' campaign has successfully compromised over 5,500 GitHub repositories by injecting malicious code. This large-scale supply chain attack poses a significant risk to developers and organizations relying on the affected repositories.

articles.title: First VPN Dismantled in Global Takedown Over Use by 25 Ransomware Groups
articles.summary: Authorities in Europe and North America dismantled a criminal VPN service that facilitated ransomware, data theft, and other cyberattacks for at least 25 different threat groups. The operation was led by law enforcement in France and the Netherlands.

articles.title: Netherlands seizes 800 servers of hosting firm enabling cyberattacks
articles.summary: Dutch financial crime investigators arrested two individuals and seized 800 servers from a hosting provider identified as a hub for cyberattacks, disinformation, and digital interference. The operation marks a significant disruption to infrastructure used to facilitate global malicious activities.

articles.title: Ghostwriter Targets Ukraine Government Entities with Prometheus Phishing Malware
articles.summary: The Belarus-aligned threat actor Ghostwriter is conducting phishing campaigns against Ukrainian government entities by leveraging lures related to the Prometheus online learning platform. The activity has been identified and reported by CERT-UA.

articles.title: Former US execs plead guilty to aiding tech support scammers
articles.summary: Two former executives pleaded guilty to facilitating a global tech support fraud scheme by hiding the illicit activities of their clients. The case highlights how corporate entities can be leveraged to sustain large-scale cyber-fraud operations.

articles.title: Why the Supreme Court's Chatrie case could change the meaning of privacy in America
articles.summary: The Supreme Court's evaluation of the Chatrie case regarding geofence searches has the potential to fundamentally redefine privacy rights and legal standards for digital surveillance in the United States.

articles.title: Canadian man arrested, charged for running KimWolf DDos botnet
articles.summary: Canadian national Jacob Butler has been arrested and charged for operating the KimWolf botnet, a DDoS-for-hire service that compromised over one million devices globally. The investigation, led by the U.S. Justice Department, highlights the ongoing crackdown on illicit cybercriminal services.

articles.title: $20 per zero-day is already the WordPress plugin reality
articles.summary: Researchers have developed an automated AI-driven pipeline capable of discovering zero-day vulnerabilities in WordPress plugins at a cost of only $20 per bug. This advancement highlights the growing efficiency of AI in vulnerability research and the potential for a surge in mass-produced software exploits.

articles.title: Authorities arrest 23-year-old accused of running the Kimwolf botnet
articles.summary: Canadian authorities arrested 23-year-old Jacob Butler for allegedly operating the Kimwolf DDoS botnet, with the United States currently seeking his extradition to face criminal charges.

articles.title: 5,561 GitHub Repositories Hit by Megalodon Supply Chain Attack in Six Hours
articles.summary: The Megalodon supply chain attack compromised over 5,500 GitHub repositories within six hours by injecting malicious CI workflows to steal cloud credentials. Researchers at SafeDep discovered the incident, highlighting a significant automated threat to software supply chains.

articles.title: Trend Micro warns of Apex One zero-day exploited in the wild
articles.summary: Trend Micro has released a security update to address a zero-day vulnerability in its Apex One software that is currently being exploited in the wild to target Windows systems.

articles.title: Drupal: Critical SQL injection flaw now targeted in attacks
articles.summary: Drupal has issued a warning that a critical SQL injection vulnerability is currently being actively exploited by attackers. Users are urged to patch their systems immediately to mitigate the risk of compromise.

articles.title: Why Chargebacks are Just One Piece of the Fraud Puzzle
articles.summary: This article explains that financial fraud extends beyond simple chargebacks to include issues like account takeovers and false declines, necessitating a more comprehensive approach to risk management. It advocates for greater visibility to protect both revenue and customer trust.

articles.title: Tracking Iranian APT Screening Serpens’ 2026 Espionage Campaigns
articles.summary: Unit 42 reports that the Iranian APT group Screening Serpens is leveraging AppDomainManager hijacking and new RAT variants to target organizations in the technology and defense sectors. The campaigns demonstrate the group's ongoing evolution in espionage tactics.

articles.title: Deleted Google API keys keep working for up to 23 minutes, researchers warn
articles.summary: Researchers discovered that Google API keys remain functional for up to 23 minutes after deletion, potentially allowing attackers to exploit leaked credentials even after revocation. This delay exposes services and sensitive data to unauthorized access during the window before the key is fully invalidated.

articles.title: Ubiquiti patches three max severity UniFi OS vulnerabilities
articles.summary: Ubiquiti has addressed three critical vulnerabilities in its UniFi OS that could allow unprivileged remote attackers to compromise affected systems. Users are encouraged to apply the released security updates immediately to mitigate potential exploitation.

articles.title: Megalodon GitHub Attack Targets 5,561 Repos with Malicious CI/CD Workflows
articles.summary: An automated campaign dubbed Megalodon injected malicious GitHub Actions workflows into over 5,500 repositories within six hours using forged identities to exfiltrate CI environment secrets. The attackers utilized base64-encoded payloads to compromise the software supply chain through automated commits.

articles.title: Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware - The BYOVD Perspective
articles.summary: This article explores techniques for interacting with Windows kernel mode drivers from user mode, specifically focusing on how to exploit vulnerabilities in drivers that are typically hardware-gated. It aims to assist security researchers in evaluating the exploitability of kernel-level findings without requiring the associated hardware.

articles.title: Techie claims Trump Mobile website was leaking thousands of people's data
articles.summary: A security researcher discovered that the Trump Mobile website was improperly configured, allowing unauthorized access to thousands of customers' sensitive personal data through simple HTTP requests.

articles.title: Kore.ai unveils AI-native platform for enterprise multiagent systems
articles.summary: Kore.ai has launched its new Artemis edition platform, designed to enable enterprises to build, govern, and deploy multiagent AI systems on Microsoft Azure. The platform emphasizes rapid deployment while integrating operational control and observability features.

articles.title: Suspected KimWolf botnet admin arrested over DDoS-for-hire operation
articles.summary: Canadian authorities arrested Jacob Butler, the alleged operator of the KimWolf botnet, which compromised over one million devices to facilitate DDoS-for-hire attacks. He is now facing charges in the United States following an extradition process.

articles.title: Versa extends zero trust principles to AI agents and MCP workflows
